subject: Post-demo qualification: SDK auth, routing & dedicated capacity sizing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@vertislabs.com>, Tom Klein <tom.klein@vertislabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo qualification: SDK auth, routing & dedicated capacity sizing

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear context on the search/qa use case and the reranker/embeddings path. Quick recap + asks so we can size a recommended Dedicated configuration and draft the mutual action plan: 

1) Integration surface
- SDK & auth: you plan to use server-side SDK calls from a small inference service (Go). Will you authenticate via short-lived tokens (STS) or a shared service account key? If STS, we’ll provide example flow.
- Routing: you want region-based routing + a fallback to a cheaper model variant during peak. Confirm primary region = us-west (SFO).
- Structured tool-calling: you’ll use a mix of tool calls for product catalog lookups. We should confirm expected average tokens/tool-call frequency.

2) Models & scoring
- Embeddings for retrieval + light reranking (candidate set ~50 per query). Estimate: 800 queries/minute peak, 95% within 300ms P50 target.

3) Dedicated capacity asks
- Target SLO: 300ms P50 gen for short prompts, 95th <= 800ms for reranker paths.
- Autoscale expectations: burst to 2x baseline for 10 min windows during ingest jobs.
- Concurrency & queues: want guidance on per-GPU concurrency, queue depth, and backpressure behavior.

Action items / next steps
- Asha/Tom: confirm auth approach (STS vs service account) and peak qps distribution (80/20 reads vs rerank).
- Ben: can you draft a capacity worksheet with suggested GPU counts, queue configs, and autoscale policy?
- Marissa / SE: prepare a short SDK snippet showing token flow + example structured tool-call payload.

I attached a blank capacity worksheet (vertis-capacity-worksheet-v1.xlsx) — please prefill the QPS and candidate sizes you expect. We’ll run numbers and come back with 2 capacity options (baseline + 2x burst).

Thanks — small follow-up call Friday if that works? I’ll coordinate times once you confirm the auth approach.

— Jonas

Thanks Jonas — good summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Auth: we prefer STS short-lived tokens (rotate daily). Our infra team runs everything in AWS (EKS) and we can swap a pod identity/token broker.
- Region: confirmed SFO primary; backup in us-east for DR.
- Workload: projected baseline ~420 qpm (queries per minute) for search retrieval; reranker invoked for ~15% of requests (~63 qpm), candidate set avg 40. Peak can go to ~900 qpm during marketing spikes (10–15 minutes).
- Latency: 300ms P50 is ideal for retrieval; reranker 95th target 750ms.

Security: please send the security questionnaire answers and any SOC2 evidence we can review while you size. Tom will fill out the worksheet this afternoon.

We’re available Friday 10–11 PT for a 30-minute follow-up if that fits your calendar.

Asha Raman
Head of Platform Engineering, Vertis Labs

Subject: Re: Post-demo qualification: SDK auth, routing & dedicated capacity sizing

Asha / Tom —

Thanks for the numbers — very helpful. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and sketched recommendations in the attached worksheet; high-level notes below: 

- Recommended baseline: 4x A100-class GPUs in Dedicated (model variant = rdx-medium-quant) with continuous batching tuned for short prompts. That gets you ~500–550 qpm retrieval capacity with low tail latency and room for autoscale.
- Reranker path: recommend dedicating 1 GPU for fast reranking or enabling a hot pool with prewarmed workers; 40 candidates @ 63 qpm maps to ~1.2k candidate-evals/minute. With quantized reranker kernels you should have headroom on the hot pool; we recommend concurrency limit of 6 per GPU for rerankers and queue depth 32.
- Autoscale: target step-scaling policy — add 2 GPUs at 60% sustained CPU/token utilization for 3 minutes, remove 1 GPU after 10 minutes of low utilization. Configure burst capacity (+2 GPUs) for scheduled marketing spikes.
- Queues & backpressure: shard queues by route (retrieval vs reranker vs tool-calls), set per-route max inflight = concurrency * num_workers and a hard rejection / retry header so callers can degrade gracefully. Example header: X-Redwood-Priority: low|normal|high.

Security notes: we support STS token exchange; see short sample flow in the linked Drive doc. I attached the worksheet with two scenarios (baseline & 2x burst) and an ops playbook stub.

Next steps:
- Asha/Tom: confirm whether reranker will be called synchronously in-path or as an async worker (affects concurrency model).
- Jonas: please schedule Friday slot 10–10:30 PT; I’ll bring a short Ops slide for the autoscale knobs.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
